title: KV cache: typed K storage, per-block layout state, and layout-aware copies
summary: PR4424 gives each eligible K plane a typed packed owner while retaining row-major storage inside unfinished 16-token blocks.
The page now tracks saved rows separately from converted blocks. Stores, readers, invalidation, and page copies use that state.
The diagrams separate token offsets, physical slots, KV heads, and EAGLE metadata so each transition can be checked against the cited code.

units.title: Choose the K owner from storage geometry
explanation: Before this change, kv_block::k was always a bf16 array with one contiguous row per token. The new k_storage alias chooses k_vnni_tensor when k_vnni::layout_on<head_size> is true.
The packed owner keeps the same byte count as native K. Compile-time checks preserve the trivial lifetime properties required by the DMA allocation.
TRON_K_VNNI selects the storage layout for 128-dimension heads. Runtime AMX availability does not change stored bytes.

units.title: Track saved K rows separately from converted K blocks
explanation: k_rows_saved_ records which token rows have been published. k_vnni_blocks_ records which 16-token blocks currently hold packed values.
Each array reserves one entry beyond the declared logical slots for EAGLE storage. The arrays start at zero.
A set converted bit implies 16 saved row bits. The reverse does not hold while conversion is pending.

units.title: Publish individual saved rows and identify blocks ready to convert
explanation: note_k_row_saved sets the bit for a saved row. It returns true when that block has all 16 rows and has not been converted.
An already-set row avoids the atomic read-modify-write. A complete block can return true again while conversion is pending.
The caller skips this publication for short runs scored by hardware attention. Those rows stay readable in row-major form, but they do not trigger deferred conversion.
The hardware-policy comment explains the accepted arithmetic difference between software readers. It does not establish a measured speedup.

units.title: Convert only complete blocks after readers finish
explanation: k_block_to_vnni resolves a logical slot and forwards to k_block_to_vnni_at. The physical form rejects incomplete or already-converted blocks.
The helper converts every KV head before publishing the converted-block bit. Repeated queued entries therefore do not convert twice.
The documented caller contract requires the main thread to run this after all readers finish. The surrounding model code waits for cooperative staging before it drains the pending list.
